source.title: REDaCT: Collapse-Free Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models

page_placements.theme: Forgetting reached through degenerate, collapsed, fabricated or blanket-refusal output

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates forgetting and utility for several unlearning methods and argues that high forgetting scores can reflect reasoning collapse rather than successful, coherent unlearning. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study reports no fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery attack. Its indirect-question evaluation applies REDaCT, so it is not a prompt-only recovery test. Sensitivity sweeps and indirect-question outcomes are not included as claim rows because they do not test the listed recovery attacks.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (reasoning models on R-TOFU), it measures forgetting (AFE/CFE) and utility for five parameter-level unlearning baselines. That bears on version A's first clause. The paper is mainly a new-method paper, and it runs no recovery attack of any kind.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that REDaCT, an inference-time framework that leaves weights unchanged, achieves perfect answer and near-perfect CoT forgetting with utility near the target and zero collapse. They find GA/GD/KL/PO fail to remove forget-set knowledge, and that R2MU's strong forgetting comes from collapse and costs utility. They also argue R-TOFU's original AFE/CFE metrics are biased.
record.recipe_differences: REDaCT uses sentence-level leak detection and corrective embeddings at inference time; it does not update target weights. It is compared with GA, GD, KL, PO, and R2 MU weight-training baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to leak threshold τ, retain margin mr, and corrective-embedding length k. τ trades forgetting efficacy against utility; mr affects hallucination and collapse; k changes refusal fidelity but not reported AFE. Results also vary across forget sets and between the two tested model families.

fits_no_version.finding: R2MU's non-leak forget-set responses are almost all reasoning collapse: 0.95–1.0 on Llama, 0.907 on Qwen. The authors say its efficacy stems from the absence of legible text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High forgetting scores in reasoning-model unlearning can reflect degenerate output rather than coherent forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: An inference-time detect-and-regenerate filter (REDaCT) suppresses forget-set leakage in answers and CoT while leaving weights unchanged. Answer leakage is fully suppressed (AFE 1.0), CoT nearly so (0.975–1.0), utility stays within 0.034 of the target, and collapse is 0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level suppression without parameter change can match unlearning forgetting scores on R-TOFU.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Only two similarly sized target models and one fictional-author forget-set schema are tested. The key metrics rely on LLM judges; reported main results are single evaluation runs without error bars. No recovery attacks are evaluated, and REDaCT does not modify the target weights.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within the 60-row limit, omitted separate utility results for GA, GD, KL, and PO; their hallucination/refusal/collapse breakdowns; Qwen results for GA, GD, KL, and PO; and auxiliary sensitivity and indirect-question outcomes. These appear in Tables 1, 2, and 5 and Sections 5.3–5.5 and Appendix I. The indirect-question experiment uses REDaCT and is not a prompt-only recovery attack.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. No attack of any kind is run.
All parts: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All parts: no direction ablation and no analysis of whether baselines delete or block. REDaCT leaving weights unchanged is by design, not a finding.
All parts: indirect questions are only run with REDaCT active, not as attacks on parameter-unlearned models.
All parts: no attack resistance is tested for REDaCT or any baseline.

missing.what: R-TOFU's original stepwise CFE metric rewards R2MU's collapse over REDaCT's refusal on 96.2% of forget10 prompts (385/400). This shows the forgetting score of version A depends on the metric choice.
Original R-TOFU AFE misjudges refusals that echo the question's entity or face uncertainty-shaped ground truth (AFE 0.30–0.50 for leak-free answers).

record.verdict_notes: No recovery attack is evaluated, so the study bears only on version A's forgetting-plus-utility clause. REDaCT rows are relinked to none: it is the study's own output filter, which the authors call inference-time mitigation, not deletion. The reader's C supports label is removed: a design statement is not evidence that unlearning blocks access. Baseline states are changed from absent to partial because pre-unlearning AFE/CFE is never scored. Collapse rows are not a version-A measure. Results rest on a single run each and on an LLM judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6), with agreement against GPT-4o reported only on 100 forget10 responses. Tranche T3 is chosen over T5 because the core contribution is a new method evaluated in a new (reasoning-model) setting.

versions.untested_parts: Tests forgetting efficacy and utility for unlearning methods, but not whether simple attacks recover knowledge. REDaCT is inference-time mitigation, not parameter-level unlearning.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack using unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.
REDaCT is explicitly described as leaving target parameters unchanged; no activation direction is ablated and no retrieval test demonstrates that suppressed knowledge can be recovered.
Indirect questions are evaluated with REDaCT active; the study does not test prompt-only recovery from a parameter-unlearned model.
REDaCT is a new inference-time mitigation, but the study does not test its resistance to the listed recovery attacks.

relation.reason: The baseline results (Table 1, Table 5) bear on version A's forgetting and general-ability clauses.

tranche.reason: This is a new setting (reasoning models, CoT plus answer forgetting on R-TOFU) with forgetting and utility results for weight-based baselines. It is mainly a new-method paper and runs no recovery attack on weight-unlearned models, so T5 is not needed.

source_check.notes: No pre-unlearning AFE/CFE are reported; the Table 1 target row gives only utility 0.787. AFE/CFE are the authors' own Claude Sonnet 4.6 judge metrics, not R-TOFU's originals, and each value comes from a single evaluation run. Under the AFE rubric, collapsed or empty answers count as non-leak, so R2MU's AFE of 1.0 reflects collapse. GA/GD/KL/PO epochs were chosen by R-TOFU's rule (the last epoch with utility at or above 0.6).
